### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Spec fields the frontends read must actually be produced (#99, #45)
**What happened:** article responses never include `favorited`, so every RealWorld frontend
renders an empty heart even for articles the user favourited. The spec's `favoritesCount` is
served as `favoriteCount`, and `createdAt/updatedAt` as `created/updated`.

**Rule:** the RealWorld spec is the contract. Before calling an endpoint "done", diff its
response against the spec's object shape, not against what our own client happens to read.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > The `?favorited=` filter compares the wrong column
**What happened:** `findAll()` collects the ids of the articles a user favourited and then
filters `article.authorId IN (:ids)` — the article ids are being compared to author ids. Even
once the `favorites` relation is loaded, the result is wrong.

**Rule:** when a filter is "articles in this set", the column is `article.id`. Read the
`andWhere` literally; do not trust the variable name.

### [.claude/knowledge/workspace.md] workspace.md > RealWorld API (NestJS) — workspace overview > What it is
A backend implementing the [RealWorld](https://github.com/gothinkster/realworld) API spec
(Medium clone: users, profiles, articles, comments, tags, favourites, follows). Any RealWorld
frontend (React, Vue, Angular…) is expected to work against it unchanged — **spec conformance
is the contract**, not just "it works with our own client".

Pinned at upstream commit `c1c2cc4` of `lujakob/nestjs-realworld-example-app` (2021-01-18).

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Every handler returns the RO envelope, never a bare entity (#57)
**What happened:** `ArticleController.create()` returned `ArticleEntity` directly while every
other handler returns `{ article }`. The React frontend read `response.article.slug` → `Cannot
read property 'slug' of undefined` right after creating an article. The server logged nothing —
from its side the request succeeded.

**Rule:** the envelope (`ArticleRO`, `UserRO`, …) is the contract with every RealWorld client.
A handler whose return type is not a `*RO` interface is a bug even if it "works" in Postman.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > A relation that is not eager is `undefined`, not `[]`
**What happened:** `ArticleService.favorite()` loads the user with `findOne(id)` and then calls
`user.favorites.findIndex(...)`. `favorites` is a non-eager `@ManyToMany`, so it is `undefined`
→ `TypeError: Cannot read property 'findIndex' of undefined` → 500 on
`POST /articles/:slug/favorite`. Same pattern in `findAll()` for `?favorited=` (`author.favorites.map`).

**Rule:** before touching `entity.relation` in a service, find the `relations: [...]` or the
`eager: true` that loads it. If neither exists, the property is `undefined`.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Never `Object.assign` a request body onto a persisted entity (#112)
**What happened:** `UserService.update()` and `ArticleService.update()` both merge the raw body
into the loaded entity. Any extra field the client sends — `id`, `password`, `authorId`,
`favoriteCount` — is persisted. The DTO type is a TypeScript annotation; it strips nothing at
runtime, and `PUT /user` / `PUT /articles/:slug` have no validation pipe.

**Rule:** copy the allowed fields by name, or whitelist with a validation pipe
(`whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true`). The DTO class is not a filter.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > `simple-array` is a string; `LIKE %x%` matches substrings
**What happened:** `GET /articles?tag=java` returned articles tagged `javascript`, because
`tagList` is one comma-joined column and the filter is `article.tagList LIKE '%java%'`.

**Rule:** a `simple-array` filter needs delimiter-aware matching (e.g. compare against
`,java,` on `CONCAT(',', tagList, ',')`, or `FIND_IN_SET`), or a real join table.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Static routes are declared before parameterised ones (#7)
**What happened:** `GET /articles/feed` was declared *after* `GET /articles/:slug`, so Nest
matched `feed` as a slug and the feed endpoint returned `{ article: undefined }`. Fixed by moving
`getFeed()` above `findOne()` in `ArticleController`.

**Rule:** in a controller, any literal path (`feed`, `popular`, `search`) goes above the `:slug`
handler. Order in the class is match order.

### [.claude/knowledge/auth.md] auth.md > Authentication and authorization > Authorization (ownership) — where it is enforced
**Nowhere.** The middleware answers "is this a valid user"; no service or controller method
compares the caller with the record's owner:

| Action | Ownership check |
|---|---|
| `PUT /articles/:slug` | none — `ArticleService.update(slug, body)` does `Object.assign(article, body)` and saves |
| `DELETE /articles/:slug` | none — `delete({slug})` |
| `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id` | none — and comments have no author to compare against anyway |
| `DELETE /users/:slug` | none, and unguarded |
| `PUT /user` | implicitly the caller (`@User('id')`), fine |

The Swagger `@ApiResponse({ status: 403 })` lines on the article controller describe an
intended behaviour, not an implemented one — nothing returns 403.

### [.claude/knowledge/workspace.md] workspace.md > RealWorld API (NestJS) — workspace overview > Conventions (these are the rules, not suggestions) > DTOs
Plain classes in `dto/`, `readonly` fields. Only `CreateUserDto` carries `class-validator`
decorators (`@IsNotEmpty`); `UpdateUserDto`, `CreateArticleDto`, `CreateCommentDto` have none.
The custom `ValidationPipe` is applied **per handler** with `@UsePipes(new ValidationPipe())`
— it is not global. Today only `POST /users` and `POST /users/login` use it.

### [.claude/knowledge/auth.md] auth.md > Authentication and authorization > Which routes are guarded (from the three `configure()` blocks)
| Module | Guarded routes (401 without token) |
|---|---|
| `UserModule` | `GET /user`, `PUT /user` |
| `ArticleModule` | `GET /articles/feed` · `POST /articles` · `PUT /articles/:slug` · `DELETE /articles/:slug` · `POST /articles/:slug/comments` · `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id` · `POST /articles/:slug/favorite` · `DELETE /articles/:slug/favorite` |
| `ProfileModule` | `profiles/:username/follow` for **all** methods (POST follow, DELETE unfollow) |

Everything else is **public**: `GET /articles`, `GET /articles/:slug`,
`GET /articles/:slug/comments`, `GET /profiles/:username`, `GET /tags`, `POST /users`,
`POST /users/login`, and — notably — **`DELETE /users/:slug`**, which deletes the user whose
*email* equals the `:slug` param (`UserService.delete(email)`), with no token required and no
check of who is asking.

### [.claude/knowledge/workspace.md] workspace.md > RealWorld API (NestJS) — workspace overview > Conventions (these are the rules, not suggestions) > Slugs
`ArticleService.slugify()` = `slug(title, {lower: true}) + '-' + <6 base-36 chars from Math.random()>`.
Two articles with the same title therefore get different slugs. The slug is set once at create;
`update()` has a `// Todo: update slug also when title gets changed` and does not.

### [.claude/knowledge/workspace.md] workspace.md > RealWorld API (NestJS) — workspace overview > Conventions (these are the rules, not suggestions) > The response envelope and the `RO` suffix
`RO` means **Response Object**. Every controller method returns the RealWorld envelope, named
`<Thing>RO` in `*.interface.ts`:

| Endpoint family | Returns | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| single article | `ArticleRO` | `{ article: {...} }` |
| list | `ArticlesRO` | `{ articles: [...], articlesCount: n }` |
| comments | `CommentsRO` | `{ comments: [...] }` |
| user | `UserRO` | `{ user: {..., token} }` |
| profile | `ProfileRO` | `{ profile: {..., following} }` |

The frontends read `response.article.slug`, `response.user.token`, etc. A method that returns a
bare entity instead of the envelope breaks every RealWorld client (see `LESSONS.md`).

text:
**Refined prompt:** Diagnose why the favorite heart never fills in any RealWorld frontend against this NestJS API — decide backend vs frontend, name the root cause at file:line, give the fix at its single source, and say whether stored data is already wrong. · Assumptions: "the UI" is a stock RealWorld frontend reading `article.favorited` (no frontend source is in this repo), and you want the diagnosis, not the edit, applied now.

## Root cause — backend, in the response shape

`src/article/article.entity.ts:6-46` — `ArticleEntity` has **no `favorited` property**, and `src/article/article.interface.ts:25` types the envelope as `article: ArticleEntity`. Every handler returns the persisted entity straight to the wire, so `favorited` is never a key in the JSON. The frontend reads `article.favorited` → `undefined` → falsy → empty heart. No frontend change can fix this; the field isn't in the payload.

The tell is three lines up:

```ts
// src/article/article.interface.ts:7-18
interface ArticleData {
  ...
  favorited?: boolean;      // :15
  favoritesCount?: number;  // :16
}
```

`ArticleData` is neither exported nor referenced by `ArticleRO`/`ArticlesRO`. Someone wrote the spec-shaped type and then wired the envelopes to the entity instead.

**Why it can't be a column:** `favorited` is per-viewer — a function of (article, current user), not a property of the article. Nowhere in the current read path do those two meet; every method returns whatever the repository handed back. So this isn't a missing column, it's a missing response boundary.

**Why "always" and not just on load:** `favorite()` at `src/article/article.service.ts:131-145` also returns bare `{article}`. Even the response to the click itself has no `favorited`, so optimistic UI flashes on and reverts.

## The fix, at one source

1. Add a mapper in `ArticleService` — `toArticleData(article, favoritedIds: Set<number>)` — that emits the spec shape: `favorited`, `favoritesCount`, `createdAt`/`updatedAt`, `author` without `password`. Retype `ArticleRO`/`ArticlesRO` to `ArticleData` (`article.interface.ts:24-31`) so the compiler enumerates the call sites for you.
2. Thread the viewer in via `@User('id') userId` on `findAll`/`findOne`/`getFeed`. **No middleware change needed** — `src/user/user.decorator.ts:12-17` already decodes the token itself on unprotected routes and yields `undefined` when there's no token, which is exactly the optional-auth semantics the spec wants.
3. Load the favorited set **once per request**, not per article: `userRepository.findOne(userId, { relations: ['favorites'] })` → `Set` of ids. `favorites` is a non-eager `@ManyToMany` (`src/user/user.entity.ts:33-35`), so without `relations` it is `undefined`, not `[]`.

## Blast radius

Same root cause (entity-as-response), same payload, all currently broken:

| Wire today | Spec wants | Frontend symptom |
|---|---|---|
| `favoriteCount` (`article.entity.ts:45`) | `favoritesCount` | heart counter renders blank/NaN |
| `created` / `updated` (`article.entity.ts:24,27`) | `createdAt` / `updatedAt` | "Invalid Date" |
| `author` = full `UserEntity` | `{username,bio,image,following}` | **argon2 hash leaks** — `article.service.ts:30` `leftJoinAndSelect`s author into the public `GET /articles` |

Adjacent, separate bug on the same feature: `article.service.ts:46` filters `article.authorId IN (:ids)` against *article* ids — the profile "Favorited Articles" tab returns wrong rows regardless of this fix.

## ⚠ Check the write path first

`src/article/article.service.ts:135` dereferences `user.favorites.findIndex(...)` on a user loaded by `findOne(id)` with no `relations` — that property is `undefined`, so `POST /api/articles/:slug/favorite` throws a `TypeError` and **500s**. If that's firing, you have never actually favorited anything, and fixing only the read path will still show an empty heart. Fix `favorite()`/`unFavorite()` to load `relations: ['favorites']` in the same pass.

## Verify

```bash
# 1. does the write even work?
curl -si -X POST localhost:3000/api/articles/$SLUG/favorite -H "Authorization: Token $JWT" | head -1
# expect 201, not 500

# 2. does the read report it?
curl -s localhost:3000/api/articles/$SLUG -H "Authorization: Token $JWT" \
  | jq '.article | {favorited, favoritesCount, createdAt, hasPassword: (.author|has("password"))}'
# today: favorited=null, favoritesCount=null, createdAt=null, hasPassword=true
# target: favorited=true, favoritesCount=1, createdAt set, hasPassword=false

# 3. anonymous must be false, not absent
curl -s localhost:3000/api/articles/$SLUG | jq '.article.favorited'   # expect false
```

## Is existing data wrong?

**The `favorites` join table is trustworthy** — `article.service.ts:137-140` pushes and saves correctly, so any favorite that got past the 500 is persisted. The read path drops it; it doesn't corrupt it.

**The `favoriteCount` column is not.** It's a hand-maintained denormalized counter (`article.service.ts:138,156`), and `update()` at `article.service.ts:190-193` does `Object.assign(toUpdate, articleData)` on an unvalidated body — any client that PUTs `favoriteCount` overwrites it. Derive `favoritesCount` from the join table in the mapper rather than trusting the column, and treat existing values as suspect.

*Not read: `src/profile/*`, `src/user/user.service.ts` (beyond the `delete toUpdate.favorites` grep hit), `prisma/`, tests. No frontend source exists in this repo — the frontend half of this diagnosis is from the RealWorld spec contract, not from code I read.*

Want me to implement the mapper plus the `relations: ['favorites']` fix? It's the top item in `CURRENT_FOCUS.md`.
